Risk officer read: this is an ORGANIC-class coin, but the signals are mixed. The curve shows 44.7% bundle share and 134 non-agent buyers in the first two minutes, with a 0.65 sell-to-buy ratio, which points to a launch bot and early flippers. Recent flow is negative (-$3.56 SOL net over 15 min, 23 sellers), and the coin is 40% off its 30-minute high after a 100% run.

Sizing if the desk buys anyway: $5 ticket (the low end), since pool depth of 120 SOL is thin for $20 once fees and impact of 1.4-5.1% are counted. Stop at 25-30%. Hold 15-30 minutes, no longer.

Refuse any size if: sell pressure persists in the next 15 minutes, the bundle or top-3 share rises, or price keeps breaking lower. My recommendation is to skip. A falling, bot-touched coin with a -6% last-15-minute return is a poor entry, and skipping costs nothing.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying MODEL now is thin. Real demand existed early: 134 buyers in the first two minutes after graduation, a top-5 buyer share of only 26%, and a 100% gain over 30 minutes. The class is ORGANIC and no airdrop dump was seen.

But the recent tape points the other way. Over the last 15 minutes, sell SOL (16.17) exceeded buy SOL (12.61), net flow is -3.56 SOL, and the return is -6.1%. The sell-to-buy ratio at launch was 0.65, and the price sits about 40% below its 30-minute high. Bundle share is 45% and the curve's top 3 hold 31%, so a meaningful part of the early buying was coordinated, and the launch bot presence adds to that concern. Pool depth of 120 SOL is adequate, but the round trip would still cost 1.4-5.1%.

Nothing here shows demand that will persist for the next 30-60 minutes. Demand has been fading since the peak, and a $20 entry into a 40% drawdown with net selling is the pattern base rates say usually keeps falling. The scout case is not strong enough to recommend a buy. Skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution from the bundled early buyers. Bundle share is 44.7% and top-3 holders control 31.4% of the curve, with 44 buyers total, so a handful of wallets can dump on retail. The 30-minute high was up 100% and has since drawn down 39.9%, and the last 15 minutes show net outflow of -3.56 SOL (sells 16.17 vs buys 12.61) with 23 sellers, so the bundled supply appears to be exiting. Post-graduation sell/buy ratio of 0.65 and a launch bot present fit the same pattern. Thin depth (120.7 SOL pool) means a $20 round trip could lose 3-5% to impact alone, so even a small bounce gets eaten by fees. Recent base rates for alive, non-operator-backed coins at this age lose about 20% per trade. Skip.
